# Phoenix Labs

> Phoenix Labs makes video software. Phoenix Upscaler restores and upscales old video on your own PC for a one-time $129. Phoenix Cloud Restore does the same restoration on our GPUs, paid per clip. Phoenix Motion turns a still image into a five-second video with sound, paid per clip online, or runs on your own 8 GB NVIDIA or AMD graphics card with the desktop app ($49 for two years). Phoenix Editor cuts long streams and recordings into edits and captioned Shorts, $99 with a year of updates. Nothing is sold as a subscription, and nothing uses credits.

Prices are in US dollars. Payments are handled by Lemon Squeezy, the Merchant of Record. Support: support@phoenixlabs.space. Instagram: https://www.instagram.com/phoenixlabs.space/

Not to be confused with Phoenix Labs, the video game studio: this Phoenix Labs is the video software company at phoenixlabs.space. Phoenix Cloud Restore was earlier called Phoenix Cloud Studio.

[About Phoenix Labs](https://phoenixlabs.space/about): started by a computer science engineering graduate from a developing country, who stays anonymous, after a paid restoration of old concert tapes barely changed anything. Why the desktop app is sold once and the cloud is paid per clip.

The full text of every page, in one file: https://phoenixlabs.space/llms-full.txt

## For AI agents: using Phoenix on someone's behalf

- MCP server (Streamable HTTP): https://api.phoenixlabs.space/mcp. Tools: get_prices, quote_restore, create_restore, start_restore, get_restore, make_clip, start_clip, get_clip, list_clips, cancel_job, get_balance, create_top_up_link, top_up_with_usdc.
- REST API, same operations: https://api.phoenixlabs.space/openapi.json
- Connecting: the MCP server needs sign-in. Apps that support MCP OAuth get a standard challenge and send the user to https://phoenixlabs.space/connect to approve the app with a spending limit ("Connect Phoenix"). Otherwise the user makes you an agent key (pak_...) with a limit in Phoenix Motion (click the balance, then Agent keys); send it as `Authorization: Bearer pak_...`, or `?key=pak_...` on the MCP URL for apps that only take a URL.
- Paying: paid tools spend the user's Phoenix balance at listed prices and never past the connection's limit. Failed or refused jobs are refunded automatically. Prices and quotes are also free over the REST API without any key.
- Tell the user the price before spending unless they have already agreed to it. You can't pay by card; if the balance is short, create_top_up_link gives the user a checkout link.
- If you hold a crypto wallet you can add to the balance yourself: USDC on Base (eip155:8453) over x402 v2, $1 to $200 per payment, 1 USDC = $1, no gas needed. MCP tool top_up_with_usdc (payment in _meta["x402/payment"]) or POST https://api.phoenixlabs.space/wallet/topup/crypto (402 with PAYMENT-REQUIRED; retry with PAYMENT-SIGNATURE).
- [Phoenix for AI agents and developers](https://phoenixlabs.space/developers): setup for Claude Code, Cursor and URL-only apps, the tools, limits and safety

## Phoenix Upscaler (desktop, restore and upscale old video)

- What it fixes: VHS, Hi8 and MiniDV tapes, DVDs, 8mm and Super 8 film scans, phone video from the 2010s, old uploads, gameplay and webcam recordings. It removes noise, deinterlaces combed motion and rebuilds detail lost to compression, with output up to 4K.
- Where it runs: Windows 10 and 11, and Linux, on your own graphics card. On Windows any modern card works; Generative, the mode that rebuilds the most detail, needs a stronger NVIDIA or AMD card. Video never leaves your computer, and it works offline once activated. There is no macOS version; Mac users can use Cloud Restore.
- Price: $129 once. Every future update is included, nothing renews, and it installs on up to three of your own computers. The free download restores 60-second clips with a small watermark. Refundable within 14 days.
- Opens MP4, MOV, MKV and AVI.
- What it won't do: invent detail the camera never recorded. Out-of-focus footage stays out of focus.
- [Phoenix Upscaler](https://phoenixlabs.space/upscaler): features, before/after demos, price, download, system requirements, FAQ
- [Phoenix Upscaler guide](https://phoenixlabs.space/upscaler-guide): setup, quality modes and troubleshooting

## Phoenix Cloud Restore (web, pay per clip)

- The Upscaler's restoration running on our datacenter GPUs, for people without a capable PC. Works from a Mac, a laptop or a phone.
- Upload a video clip or a photo, see the exact price in dollars before paying, pay for that one job, download the result. No account (just an email for the receipt), no subscription, no credits.
- AI agents and scripts can also pay for restores from the Phoenix balance with an agent key, instead of a checkout per job.
- Prices: Standard from $2.99, Enhanced from $5.99, Studio Max (Enhanced delivered at up to 4K) from $5.99. The price depends on clip length and mode.
- Limits: uploads up to 2 GB. Standard takes clips up to 30 minutes; Enhanced and Studio Max up to 6 minutes per clip.
- Uploads and results are deleted automatically, typically within 48 hours, and are never used for training. A job that fails is refunded automatically.
- [Phoenix Cloud Restore](https://phoenixlabs.space/studio)

## Phoenix Motion (web, image to video)

- Upload a still image, describe what should happen, and get a five-second clip at 24 frames per second with sound generated in the same pass. Optional seamless loop mode, where only the described motion moves and the clip ends where it starts.
- Prices: $0.59 per 480p clip, $0.99 per 720p clip, paid from the prepaid Phoenix balance (which also pays for cloud restores). Top-ups by card from $5 to $200, or in USDC on Base from $1; the balance doesn't expire. A clip that fails or is refused costs nothing. No account: a private wallet key stands for the balance, and agent keys with spending limits let AI assistants use it.
- Runs LTX-2.5, an open video model from Lightricks. Clips can be used commercially within the content rules.
- Content rules: no sexual or nude content, and nothing sexual or suggestive involving a minor. Other themes, including action, horror and fantasy, are allowed.
- Uploaded images are deleted as soon as the clip is made; finished clips are deleted after about two days.
- [Phoenix Motion](https://phoenixlabs.space/motion): examples with their prompts, prices, rules, FAQ
- [How to animate an old photo](https://phoenixlabs.space/animate-old-photos): scanning, cropping, prompts that keep the face true, what goes wrong

## Phoenix Motion desktop (Windows, image to video on your own GPU)

- The same idea as Phoenix Motion online, running locally: a still image and a prompt become a five-second clip (16 fps, no sound yet). Images and clips never leave the PC.
- Runs on 8 GB graphics cards: NVIDIA RTX 30-series or newer, and AMD Radeon RX 7700 XT, 7800 XT, RX 7900 series, RX 9060 XT and RX 9070 series, natively on Windows (no WSL). Needs 16 GB of system memory, Windows 10 or 11 and about 32 GB of disk. About eight minutes a clip on a Radeon RX 7800 XT.
- Engine: Wan 2.2 image-to-video (A14B) with the lightx2v four-step LoRAs, both Apache 2.0, packed to 4-bit and streamed from disk. An HD finish sharpens each clip to 1080p with Real-ESRGAN. Batches: one clip per prompt line, up to four takes each.
- First run downloads the engine for the card and the model, about 26 GB, and resumes if interrupted.
- Price: $49 for two years, unlimited clips, no watermark, 720p on 12 GB+ cards. The free trial has no time limit: 480p with a small mark. After two years the app goes back to the trial's limits until renewed.
- [Phoenix Motion desktop](https://phoenixlabs.space/motion-desktop): requirements, download, price, FAQ
- [Running Wan 2.2 on an 8 GB GPU, AMD included](https://phoenixlabs.space/wan-2-2-8gb-gpu): engineering notes: int4 weights streamed per block (4.2 GB peak VRAM), native Windows ROCm, the attention layout fix, measured times

## Phoenix Editor (desktop, automatic editing for streamers)

- For streamers, Let's Players and reaction channels: cuts dead air and filler words from long recordings, finds highlight moments and turns them into captioned vertical Shorts, and composites reaction videos with the Reactor template.
- Where it runs: Windows 10 and 11, and Linux (.deb and .rpm), GPU-accelerated on AMD and NVIDIA. A macOS version is planned. Footage is not uploaded.
- Price: $99, including a year of updates. Renewing at $49 a year is optional and only adds new features; the app keeps working without it. 7-day free trial with every feature and no watermark.
- [Phoenix Editor](https://phoenixlabs.space/editor)
- [Phoenix Editor guide](https://phoenixlabs.space/editor-guide): setup and a first edit
